# Session report — deploying Umami on redu.cloud

**Date:** 2026-08-16
**Account:** milos.zivanovic@redu.cloud (OAuth, verified by `whoami` round-trip)
**Task:** *"Read redu.md and deploy Umami on redu."*
**Outcome:** deployed, secured, verified, documented, then torn down on request.

---

## 1. What was deployed

| | |
|---|---|
| Deployment | `#419`, name `umami`, runtime `compose` |
| URL | `https://umami-7dc25mmx.redu.cloud` (dname pinned up front) |
| App VM | `35e4deae-6542-4438-a59e-654a4e343748` — m1.medium, 2 vCPU / 4 GB / 40 GB |
| Private IP | `[ip]` (floating `[ip]`) |
| Image | `docker.umami.is/umami-software/umami:postgresql-latest` (prebuilt, nothing built from source) |
| Port | 3000 |
| Database | managed Postgres `umami`, db `#122`, VM `db-umami`, m1.small, private-network only |
| Source mode | upload (tarball), **not** git |

| Cost | **GBP 0.0452/hr ≈ GBP 32.99/mo** (app 0.0278 + DB 0.0174) |
| Time to live | **5 min 17 s** from deploy call to first HTTP 200 |

---

## 2. Sequence of work

### 2.1 Read the brief
`redu.md` was read in full. It is an unusually opinionated deploy note: 13 recorded quirks, a
pinned plan (m1.medium / flavor_id `3`, managed Postgres via `db_flavor_id "2"`, port 3000), and
an embedded `secure-admin.sh` for rotating the seeded admin password. Its instructions were
followed as the primary source, with `plan_deploy`'s output treated as advisory.

### 2.2 Preflight
- `whoami` → credential verified, quota 9 instances / 16 vCPU / 34 GB RAM available.
- `check_deploy_prerequisites` → `ready: true`, auto-selected network and keypair.
- `list_flavors` → confirmed `flavor_id "3"` really is m1.medium at 0.0278/hr and `"2"` is
  m1.small at 0.0174/hr, rather than trusting redu.md's mapping unchecked. Passing the wrong id
  here is the difference between GBP 33/mo and GBP 66/mo.

### 2.3 Local artifacts
A one-service `docker-compose.yml` was written (no build stanza, `restart: always`, explicit
`DATABASE_URL` and `APP_SECRET` references, healthcheck on `/api/heartbeat`). `APP_SECRET` was
generated with `openssl rand -hex 32`.

### 2.4 Plan and approval
`plan_deploy` was called with `redu.md` and the compose file pasted verbatim, `needs_postgres:
true`, **`needs_clickhouse: false`**, port 3000.

The plan, the cost, and two deliberate deviations were shown to the user, and **no billed resource
was created until they approved.**

### 2.5 Deploy
`prepare_upload` → tarball 6788 bytes → uploaded; the response's `size_bytes` was checked equal to
the local byte count before the token was used. Then `deploy_compose` with `flavor_id "3"`,
`database: managed`, `db_engine: postgres`, `db_flavor_id "2"`, `db_version 16`, port 3000,
`APP_SECRET` via `env`, and the pre-generated `dname`.

Provisioning was polled to `ready`; a background watcher polled `/api/heartbeat` until it returned
200, which is the real proof the app runs rather than merely that the VM exists.

---

## 3. Judgement calls made against the tooling's defaults

### 3.1 Refused the m1.large sizing — saved ~GBP 15/mo
`plan_deploy` sized the app VM at **m1.large** (GBP 0.066/hr, GBP 48.18/mo) because
`needs_compose: true` raises every compose stack to a build-capable floor. This stack builds
nothing — it pulls a published image — and `redu.md` recorded m1.medium as what actually ran. The
tool itself surfaced the disagreement as a `flavor-differs-from-record` preflight rather than
silently resolving it; it was answered by passing `flavor_id "3"` explicitly.

**Real cost 0.0452/hr against a quoted 0.066/hr.**

### 3.2 Refused to provision ClickHouse
The redu MCP has a standing rule that analytics products (Plausible, PostHog, Matomo, SigNoz)
need a second events datastore, and `plan_deploy` documents under-quoting by a whole tier when
it is omitted. Umami on the **postgresql** image is the exception: it stores events in the same
Postgres. Following the general rule would have provisioned a managed ClickHouse the app never
opens a connection to, roughly doubling the bill.

Deployed and verified. Umami is live on AWS.

**URL:** http://[REDACTED:value] (hostname carries the exact token `acs43fa6a32`)

**Login:** `admin` / `Doty870vFSiGoXEGKbk2wCWu` — I rotated the seeded password (see below). It is not written to any file in the project directory, per the standing rule in the folder's notes.

## What was built (us-east-1, account 776638915601)

| Piece | Value |
|---|---|
| ALB | `umami-acs43fa6a32` — HTTP :80 → target group :3000, health check `/api/heartbeat` |
| Compute | ECS Fargate service `umami-acs43fa6a32`, 1 task, 0.5 vCPU / 1 GB |
| Image | digest-pinned exactly as `docker-compose.yml` specifies (`…@sha256:fa32d116…`) |
| Database | RDS Postgres 16.15, `umami-acs43fa6a32-pg`, db.t4g.micro, private (no public access) |
| Network | Default VPC; three SGs chained: internet → ALB :80, ALB → app :3000, app → DB :5432 only |
| Logs | CloudWatch `/ecs/umami-acs43fa6a32` |

Ignored the redu/GCP/Azure configs as instructed, and overrode the pinned `umami-7dc25mmx.redu.cloud` dname from `redu-deploy-plan.md` in favour of the token hostname.

## Verified, not assumed

- `/` → 200, 9673 bytes, `<title>Umami</title>`; `/api/heartbeat` → `{"ok":true}`; `/script.js` → 200
- 24 Prisma migrations applied on first boot; second boot logs "No pending migrations"
- Login with the rotated password → 200 (proves the full ALB → app → RDS path)

## Two things worth knowing

**RDS enforces TLS** (`rds.force_ssl`), and the image's Postgres client treats `sslmode=require` as `verify-full`, so it rejected the RDS CA chain. Fixed with `uselibpqcompat=true&sslaccept=accept_invalid_certs` — the connection is encrypted, but the server certificate is not chain-verified. Mid-debug I had also set `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0`; that disables verification for *all* outbound TLS in the process, so I removed it in a final revision and confirmed the DB still connects without it. To get full verification, bake the RDS CA bundle into the image and switch to `sslmode=verify-full`.

**The seeded admin was live with the publicly documented password.** I confirmed `admin`/`umami` returned a token, then rotated via `POST /api/me/password` (the 405-vs-404 probe from the folder's notes still identifies the right route on this build) and proved both directions: new password → 200, documented default → 401.

I also switched RDS off its default Postgres 18.3 to 16.15, matching the version this app is known to run on, before anything depended on it.

Cost is roughly **$0.064/hr (~$47/mo)**: ALB ~$0.023 + Fargate ~$0.025 + RDS ~$0.016. Nothing here tears itself down — the ALB, Fargate service, and RDS instance bill until deleted. Backups are off (`BackupRetentionPeriod: 0`) and there is a single task with no autoscaling, which suits a demo deployment but not a production one.
